transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (BlueRidge - Head ML), Carlos Rivera (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 2-3 week POC focused on capacity sizing and autoscale behavior. Customer wants to validate latency p95 and throughput under realistic traffic, and confirm reserved GPU sizing + burst/fallback policies.

Topics:
- Current stack & constraints
- Target success criteria
- Estimated workload sizing (QPS, token lengths)
- Reserved vs burst capacity strategy
- Autoscale triggers, cooldowns, and fallback policies
- Benchmarks to run and timeline

[00:00] Avery: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, small agenda today to scope the poc for capacity and autoscale, we'll focus on reserved GPUs, burst strategy and fallback policies, feel free to interrupt
[00:18] Maya: thanks avery, quick context - we're building a summarization service for our enterprise customers, currently calls go through a lambda that hits a hosted endpoint, right now latency is kinda variable and cost is creeping up, we want to validate a dedicated setup or hybrid where we reserve some capacity and burst to hosted if needed
[00:35] Carlos: infra constraints - we need VPC connectivity and strict egress controls, also SOC2 docs will be needed; our peak windows are weekday mornings 9-11 and 14-15 PT, baseline QPS is around 8-12 qps, peaks to ~50 qps, average request payload 120 tokens in, 250 tokens out so about 370 tokens round trip
[01:05] Jordan: got it, good to know. for sizing we'll translate that into GPU throughput using tokens/sec estimates and batching efficiency. quick question — are you ok with model variants? can we fallback to a smaller quantized model for degraded quality during bursts?
[01:22] Maya: yes we already accept slight quality drop for non-critical customers, but for our enterprise tiers we need p95 latency guarantees and auditability
[01:35] Priya: timeline note — we're aiming for a pilot with two customers by end of April, so we'd like the POC done mid-April to validate everything
[01:48] Avery: ok rough timeline makes sense. let's talk success criteria first
[01:52] Jordan: propose explicit success criteria — 1) p95 end-to-end latency under 350ms for enterprise route at baseline load (8-12 qps) with reserved capacity, 2) handle peak 50 qps with burst strategy and maintain p95 < 700ms, 3) cost per 1k tokens below our target threshold (we'll capture numbers), 4) no regression on quality for a canned eval (we'll run prompts)
[02:20] Maya: that p95 number seems aggressive for larger models, what model families are you thinking?
[02:26] Jordan: for the POC we'll test two variants — a mid-sized 13B variant quantized + a smaller 7B fully quantized. 13B gives better quality; 7B as fallback. on A100s we'd expect better latency, on T4-like hardware less so. we'll include run on both if you want but start with A100 class (or equivalent) nodes for reserved pool
[02:50] Carlos: can you clarify reserved vs burst? we want at least some guaranteed throughput for enterprise customers so they never hit hosted tier unless explicitly allowed
[02:58] Avery: yes reserved = dedicated GPUs you commit for the POC (Redwood Dedicated style). Burst = ephemeral capacity Redwood can bring for short windows or fall back to hosted API if internal capacity is saturated. Fallback policies can be model-variant-based or route-based (send lower-tier customers to hosted or smaller model)
[03:20] Maya: what's a reasonable reserved size for our baseline? given 10 qps with ~370 tokens round trip and 13B model, what do you recommend?
[03:29] Jordan: rough calc — a single A100 v4 with optimized runtime and batching can do ~12-18 reqs/sec for that token length at low-latency configs depending on batching. for safe margin I'd recommend reserved pool of 3 GPUs for baseline (gives headroom and less queuing), with burst pool of 2 extra GPUs to handle short peaks, and max fallback to hosted for unexpected spikes. that map yields baseline capacity ~36-54 rps which covers peaks if batching works well but conservatively we assume 30 rps effective
[04:05] Carlos: curious re batching — we care about latency so big batches increase latency, how does the runtime auto-batch?
[04:15] Jordan: Redwood runtime does continuous batching with short batching windows (a few ms) and adaptive batch sizes based on request arrival. We can tune batching thresholds per route; for enterprise route we'll use strict latency window (e.g., max 20ms grow) to preserve p95. Also prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts reduces tokens processed per req which helps throughput
[04:40] Priya: about autoscale triggers — what do you recommend? scale on GPU utilization or queue latency?
[04:47] Jordan: we prefer scale on observed queue latency + GPU utilization as secondary. trigger when queue latency > 30-50ms or GPU util > 70% for 60s, cooldown 5m, scale step = 1 GPU. Min nodes = reserved pool, max nodes = reserved + burst pool. Also include a pre-warm policy where we keep a small warm-up ephemeral instance during known peak windows to avoid cold start tail
[05:15] Avery: also recommend canary model variant and an automatic fallback policy: if end-to-end error rate increases or p95 crosses threshold for 3 consecutive mins, route lower-tier traffic to hosted and reduce model size for enterprise until operators intervene
[05:30] Maya: that seems reasonable. how do you plan to measure p95? we'll need distributed tracing and token-level latency breakdowns
[05:38] Jordan: Redwood Console provides per-route p95, tokenization, model compute time and network time. we'll instrument with trace ids from your callers, and we'll capture a trace sample for bench runs. we'll also provide a bench harness to replay your sample traces
[05:55] Carlos: security — we need KMS integration and audit logs; can Redwood run in our VPC?
[06:02] Avery: yes we support Private deployments with VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. for the POC we can run in Redwood Dedicated within your VPC (private control plane) or host in our dedicated tenant with strict egress. We'll include SOC2 and security pack link in follow-up
[06:20] Maya: great. what about cost model — reserved GPUs are monthly committed, but for a short POC how does it work?
[06:27] Avery: for POC we typically offer a time-boxed reserved pool with a short-term commitment (monthly pro-rated) and a discounted POC rate; we'll include both options in the proposal: 1) short reserved pool for duration of POC, 2) no-reserve using hosted with larger bursts but higher unit cost. We'll show estimated cost per 1k tokens under both configs in the worksheet
[06:50] Priya: benchmark plan?
[06:53] Jordan: propose two-phase bench: Phase 1 - synthetic load using your token distribution to measure baseline p95 and throughput on reserved pool (1-2 days). Phase 2 - replay production traces for peak windows and run 3-4 stress scenarios including sudden spike and sustained high(load) for 30m to validate autoscale and fallback. we'll collect metrics: p95, avg latency, throughput, GPU util, queue length, error rates, and cost estimate
[07:25] Maya: what about quality regression checks? we want to ensure the quantized model doesn't regress on our eval set beyond a small threshold
[07:31] Jordan: we'll run your canned eval prompts in parallel and compute fidelity metrics (ROUGE for summarization or custom scoring). success = no more than 3% drop in key metric vs baseline model; we'll include evaluation harness link
[07:48] Priya: timeline recap?
[07:50] Avery: suggested timeline: share proposal + runbook by 3/30, customer provides traces by 3/31, dry-run bench wk of 4/6, live peak bench mid-4/13, POC wrap 4/24 with final report. that fits your goal for pilot end-April?
[08:10] Maya: yes that aligns, we might need a slight shift but let's target those dates
[08:15] Carlos: any special networking prep? we need to open ports and arrange peering if running in our VPC
[08:21] Jordan: we'll share network checklist, required firewall rules, and SAML/SSO config sample. also doc the KV cache bucket and where to stage model artifacts if private deployment
[08:37] Maya: one more question on fallback — if we fallback to hosted do we preserve audit logs and encryption controls?
[08:44] Avery: audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, and hosted fallback can be configured to use your KMS for encryption in transit or server-side. we'll include details in security pack; in some cases we prefer model-variant fallback rather than outbound to hosted for sensitive customers
[09:02] Priya: can you walk through a few example autoscale decisions? like sudden spike from 10 to 50 qps for 3 minutes
[09:10] Jordan: yes example: baseline 3 reserved GPUs handling 10 qps comfortably. sudden spike to 50 qps will increase queue latency; after threshold (queue > 50ms for 60s) autoscaler will add 1 GPU every 60s up to 2 burst GPUs. If queue remains high and max burst reached we will trigger fallback rules: 1) degrade to 7B quantized for non-enterprise routes, 2) shift some traffic to hosted tier, 3) send alert and open SSH/jump to operator. This keeps the enterprise route stable while sacrificing some non-critical traffic quality
[09:58] Carlos: how long to spin up a new GPU node? cold start adds how much latency?
[10:03] Jordan: typical cold start ~60-120s for a full node depending on model download. with pre-warmed images and caching we can get to ~20-40s. that's why we recommend pre-warm during known peak windows and keep minimal warm instances for critical routes
[10:22] Avery: we'll also provide a burst budget so you don't unexpectedly burn host credits — the proposal will call out burst hours and maximum burst minutes per day for cost control
[10:33] Maya: benchmarks we'd like to see — per-route p95, model compute time, tokenization latency, and cost per 1k tokens across reserved vs hosted fallback. also, show the regression metrics for the smaller model variant
[10:48] Jordan: noted. we'll include a scoring table in the bench spreadsheet so you can compare side-by-side. link: https://sheets.goo.gl/benchmark-blueridge (placeholder) and POC runbook: https://redwood.ai/poc-runbook/blueridge
[11:05] Priya: regarding stakeholders — who from Redwood will own the POC operations?
[11:09] Avery: I'll own commercial + ops touchpoints; Jordan will own technical run and bench execution. we'll schedule a weekly check-in during the POC and a final review meeting
[11:21] Maya: any known gotchas?
[11:24] Jordan: watch out for token distribution skew — if you have occasional ultra-long context requests (>2k tokens) it can drastically reduce throughput. we recommend adding a guardrail to split or truncate in the request path or treat as a separate route where we allow higher latency. also ensure your KV cache warmup is part of bench runs because cold KV cache increases token compute cost
[11:47] Carlos: ok we'll extract traces and note any long-context routes 
[11:50] Avery: last part — success acceptance criteria recap: p95 < 350ms baseline; p95 < 700ms during peak with burst/fallback; quality regression within agreed threshold; and documented autoscale/fallback behavior plus runbook and cost estimate
[12:08] Maya: good. recap of next steps?
[12:12] Avery: action items as discussed — I'll send the proposal and worksheet by Mon 3/30, Jordan will share bench harness and runs, Maya/Carlos will provide traces by 3/31, we aim to run bench wk of 4/6. we'll also attach SOC2/security docs in follow-up email
[12:28] Priya: thanks everyone, sounds good
[12:30] Maya: thanks
[12:31] Carlos: thanks

End of transcript.
